1	\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
2	
3	ThreadGate adds per-layer gated MLP networks with an auxiliary GAR loss; training succeeds (TF GAR\,=\,0.50) but autoregressive GAR collapses 8--17$\times$ on Qwen-2.5-7B (27$\times$ on Llama-3.1-8B). Gating provides modest improvement over LoRA-only ($p$\,=\,0.004) but is insufficient to close the gap. Steering ($\beta$\,=\,5, GAR 0.727) and scheduled sampling (gap 7.8$\times$$\to$1.44$\times$; single seed) implicate attention misallocation as the proximal cause.
4

1	\section{Experiments}
2	\label{sec:experiments}
3	
4	\subsection{Setup}
5	
6	We fine-tune Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct on 8K multi-turn conversations from the UltraChat training split. Training uses 3 epochs with AdamW (lr $= 2 \times 10^{-4}$, batch size 1, gradient accumulation 8, seed 42; ThreadGate additionally with seed 123); each variant requires approximately 6 hours on a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU (102\,GB). Full hyperparameters are in Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-hyper}; the controlled comparison design is described in \S\ref{sec:comparison-design}. We evaluate under \emph{IID} (same-distribution UltraChat text) and \emph{held-out} (50 non-overlapping conversations) teacher-forced protocols, reporting GAR-ours, GAR-Dongre \citep{dongre2026attention}, and PPL.
7

19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42

Multi-turn dialogue is the dominant mode of interaction with large language models (LLMs), and system prompts that specify task goals form the foundation of instruction following. As conversations grow longer, however, models progressively lose track of these goal specifications. \citet{dongre2026attention} quantified this degradation across 12 models: the Goal Accessibility Ratio (GAR), which measures how much attention the model allocates to goal tokens in the system prompt, declines by 27--48\% between early and mid-conversation turns. We replicate and extend this finding on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, observing a 70.8\% relative decline in GAR from 0.0418 at turn~1 to 0.0122 at mid-conversation. We attribute the steeper decline partly to our use of last-token GAR, which captures summary-position attention more sensitively than the all-token average of \citet{dongre2026attention}, and partly to Qwen-2.5-7B's stronger instruction-following fidelity in early turns. This attention decay represents a systematic failure of multi-turn models to maintain task coherence, and it grows worse with each additional turn.

A striking aspect of this degradation is what it does \emph{not} affect. \citet{dongre2026attention} showed that goal-relevant information persists in the residual stream throughout the conversation: linear discriminant analysis probes recover goal content with AUC\,=\,0.98 even at late turns where attention to goal tokens has collapsed. The information is present in the hidden states, but the attention mechanism fails to route it toward the output computation. This dissociation between information availability and information utilization suggests a natural intervention point.

If the residual stream already carries goal information, a learnable gate on the residual pathway could amplify or attenuate layer contributions to recover goal attention. This reasoning motivates ThreadGate, which modulates each residual update with a content-and-turn-conditioned MLP gate: $x_{l+1} = x_l + g_l \cdot f_l(x_l)$, where $g_l$ is produced by a two-layer network conditioned on the hidden state and turn features, inspired by the residual scaling idea of ReZero \citep{bachlechner2021rezero}.

Fine-tuned to allocate 50\% of its attention to system-prompt goals (GAR\,=\,0.50 under teacher forcing), Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct retains only GAR\,=\,0.064 under autoregressive generation---an 8$\times$ collapse that widens to 27$\times$ on Llama-3.1-8B. This paper traces the failure to exposure bias \citep{bengio2015scheduled}: attention patterns optimized under teacher-forced prefixes do not transfer to model-generated text, even when next-token prediction (NTP) remains robust.

Multi-turn attention decay is well-documented---\citet{dongre2026attention} showed that the Goal Accessibility Ratio (GAR), measuring attention to system-prompt goal tokens, declines 27--48\% across 12 models (we observe 70.8\% on Qwen-2.5-7B) while residual stream probes retain goal content (AUC\,=\,0.98)---but three research gaps remain open. No work examines how per-layer transformer behavior varies across conversation turns (the \emph{turn$\times$depth} gap). Existing remediations---split-softmax \citep{li2024measuring}, StreamingLLM \citep{xiao2024streaming}, gated attention \citep{qiu2025gated}---operate at inference time or are turn-agnostic; \emph{training-time} multi-turn attention optimization is unexplored. And classical exposure bias mitigation \citep{bengio2015scheduled,lamb2016professor} targets RNN sequence generation; no \emph{multi-turn transformer equivalent} exists.

ThreadGate addresses these gaps with per-layer content-and-turn-conditioned MLP gates on the residual stream: $x_{l+1} = x_l + g_l \cdot f_l(x_l)$, where $g_l$ is a two-layer network conditioned on hidden states and turn position. A five-way controlled comparison---ThreadGate, +PCGrad, Uniform Gate, LoRA-only, Base---isolates turn conditioning, gating, gradient conflict, and fine-tuning (\S\ref{sec:comparison-design}), where each adjacent pair kills exactly one alternative hypothesis.

Our contributions: (1)~the first empirical measurement of how exposure bias selectively destroys auxiliary attention losses (8--17$\times$ on Qwen-2.5-7B, 27$\times$ on Llama-3.1-8B), establishing a failure benchmark for attention steering under teacher-forcing; (2)~PCGrad-based causal exclusion demonstrating that gradient direction conflict---despite being measurably present (68--79\% of layers)---is causally inconsequential ($p$\,=\,0.002, effect reverses); (3)~the first evidence that scheduled sampling transfers to multi-turn transformer attention objectives (gap 7.8$\times$$\to$1.44$\times$); (4)~cross-architecture validation confirming the 27$\times$ gap generalizes across model families.

\paragraph{Attention manipulation.}
StreamingLLM \citep{xiao2024streaming} identified attention sinks and proposed anchor token retention; \citet{hsieh2024found} showed positional bias against middle-positioned information; \citet{qiu2025gated} replaced softmax with a learned gate for sparse attention; Rhea \citep{hong2025rhea} introduces role-aware episodic attention for multi-turn dialogue. PASTA \citep{zhang2024tell} steers attention post-hoc by reweighting a subset of attention heads toward user-specified tokens; our $\beta$-steering applies a simpler additive bias to all layers but serves a diagnostic rather than deployment purpose. These approaches intervene inside the attention mechanism, while ThreadGate operates on the residual stream. Our results suggest that neither pathway alone overcomes the distributional gap between teacher-forced training and autoregressive inference.
